hints: Look closely at the three bullet points about primary structure. Which type of amino acid would be found buried away from water at the centre, and which type carries a full positive or negative charge?
Recall what holds tertiary structure together. Charged R groups form ionic bonds, and hydrophobic R groups cluster together in the core to avoid water.
walkthrough:
**Remember what thermostable means**

Great start. Thermostable means the tertiary structure stays folded at high temperature.

That must mean it has extra strong bonds and interactions holding the 3D shape together.

**Link charged amino acids to ionic bonds**

The enzyme has more charged amino acids than a normal enzyme.

Charged R groups with opposite charges attract to form ionic bonds, so more charged amino acids means more ionic bonds.

**Link hydrophobic amino acids to the centre**

The enzyme also has more hydrophobic amino acids.

Hydrophobic R groups avoid water and pack together by hydrophobic interactions in the centre (core) of the protein, so more hydrophobic amino acids means more amino acids interacting at the centre.

Both comparisons are more than, which is row D.

options.A: Ionic bonds are correctly more than, but centre interactions are not less than. More hydrophobic amino acids means more packing at the centre.
options.B: Both are wrongly less than. More charged amino acids gives more ionic bonds, and more hydrophobic amino acids gives more core interactions.
options.C: Centre interactions are correctly more than, but ionic bonds are not less than. More charged amino acids allows more ionic bonds to form.
options.D: Correct. More charged amino acids gives more ionic bonds, and more hydrophobic amino acids gives more hydrophobic interactions at the centre, both stabilising tertiary structure at high temperature.
